CURRENT SCENE:
他难怪抱怨，他想他的朋友，因为他不要离开他的城市。他的妈妈找到孟子一个老师。跟老师孟子学最重要的文学，所以他成为哲学家。

ITEMS:

[I141] 【他】想他的朋友   correction: 他 → (delete)   strength: error
  checker's note: 他 repeats the subject of the clause before: zero form
  rule card (zero_redundant_pronoun, Coherence: reference): When the same person or thing is already clear in the same clause or close continuation, delete the repeated subject or possessive: use zero form. In 不是……而是……, put the subject before 不是 and do not repeat it after 而是.  Pattern: <wrong> → <correct>: <subject/possessive> is already clear, so delete it; Chinese uses zero form here.  Her terms: redundant, too many他, Subj.不是……而是……, Subj. before “不是……而是……”
  her past correction: [-他]想帮他们 — her note: redundant
  her past correction: [-他]想帮忙 — her note: redundant
  her past correction: [-他]想找工作

[I142] 因为【他】不要离开他的城市   correction: 他 → (delete)   strength: error
  checker's note: 他 repeats the subject of the clause before: zero form
  rule card (zero_redundant_pronoun, Coherence: reference): When the same person or thing is already clear in the same clause or close continuation, delete the repeated subject or possessive: use zero form. In 不是……而是……, put the subject before 不是 and do not repeat it after 而是.  Pattern: <wrong> → <correct>: <subject/possessive> is already clear, so delete it; Chinese uses zero form here.  Her terms: redundant, too many他, Subj.不是……而是……, Subj. before “不是……而是……”

  her past correction: 他[回了→回到了]他的城市
  her past correction: [-他要回家]

[I143] 因为他【不要】离开他的城市   correction: 不要 → 不想   strength: error
  checker's note: 不想 means “does not want to”
  rule card (directional_complements, Grammar): Use V. + directional complement + Place + 来/去: put the place after the directional complement and before 来/去. For walking to a place, use 走到place来/去, not 走去 or 走来Place.  Pattern: <wrong> → <correct>: put the place after the directional complement; use V. + directional complement + Place + 来/去 (or 走到place来/去).  Her terms: V. + directional complement + Place + 来/去, 走到place来/去, 走去/来Place, 拿起来, 拿上去
  her past correction: 所以他们[到城市的外边搬家了→搬到城市外了]
  her past correction: 他[回了→回到了]他的城市
  her past correction: 他们搬到[+了]城市 — her note: 了completed

[I144] 他的妈妈找到【^】孟子一个老师   correction: ∅ → 给   strength: error
  checker's note: the person receiving the teacher needs 给
  rule card (redundant_words, Other): Delete words, names, time phrases, or repeated structures when they add no new meaning or repeat information already given. For example, do not add 当 after 是, and do not use two words that express the same time or idea.  Pattern: <wrong> → <correct>: <deleted part> is redundant because <the remaining word(s)> already expresses this meaning.  Her terms: redundant, redundant with是, redundant with看起来
  her past correction: [-孟子的妈妈]告诉孟子 — her note: redundant
  her past correction: 孟子的妈妈叫[-了]孟子搬家 — her note: 叫/让 is a modal verb, no了
  her past correction: 可是孟子的妈妈[+就]有别的看法 — her note: or 他有的时候跟朋友玩儿

[I145] 他的妈妈找到孟子【一个】老师   correction: 一个 → 的   strength: suggestion
  rule card (modifier_de_structure, Grammar): Use 的 after a modifier when it describes a noun, especially a longer phrase such as 人类创造的文明 or 能吃的植物. Do not add 的 after quantity words or fixed modifiers where it is not needed, such as 很多人, 一些人, 今天清晨, 蓝色衣服, and 好主意.  Pattern: <wrong> → <correct>: <modifier> describes the noun <noun>, so use 的; or <modifier> does not need 的 here, so omit it.  Her terms: no的

[I146] 【跟老师孟子】学最重要的文学   correction: 跟老师孟子 → 孟子跟老师   strength: error
  checker's note: the subject should come before 跟老师
  rule card (laoshi_negative_repetition, Vocabulary): 老是 means “always” and is used for something negative or to complain; for a neutral or positive repeated action, use 一直 or 常常 instead.  Pattern: <老是 + action> → <一直/常常 + action>: the action is neutral or positive, not something negative to complain about, so do not use 老是.  Her terms: 老是
  her past correction: 孟子[跟老师老是学习中文→一直学习中文] — her note: “老是“ for something negative, used to complain

[I147] 所以他成为【^】哲学家   correction: ∅ → 了   strength: suggestion
  rule card (le_completed, Coherence: temporality (了/着/在)): Use 了 for an action completed in the narrative or for a change of state (了completed). Do not use 了 merely because there is an action verb.  Pattern: <wrong> → <correct>: <action/change> is completed in the story, so it takes 了 (了completed).  Her terms: 了completed, 了completed/change, 着durative, 把
  her past correction: 他成为[+了]哲学家
  her past correction: 他[+后来]成为哲学家
  her past correction: 而是成为[哲学人→哲学家]

items.explanation: 他 is already clear from the close continuation, so delete it; Chinese uses zero form here.
他 is already clear from the previous clause, so it is redundant. Chinese uses zero form here.
不想 means “does not want to.” Use 不想离开他的城市 here.
Use 给 to mark 孟子 as the person receiving the teacher. Say 给孟子找了一个老师.
It would be more natural to use 的 because 孟子 describes the noun 老师: 孟子的老师.
Put the subject 孟子 before 跟老师. Say 孟子跟老师学最重要的文学.
Becoming a philosopher is a completed change in the story, so use 了completed: 成为了哲学家.
